operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: mountain=7 rows, climber=10 rows; no sampling cap needed, full read is trivial.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0: no NULLs in original, but schema permits them; TS may emit NULLs only via empty-parent FK path.
climber.Mountain_ID FK -> mountain.Mountain_ID, parent exists, parent PK unique; 5 distinct child values over 7 parents (some parents unreferenced).
climber.Time is TEXT storing race times like '1:13.05.6' (colon+dot, not HH:MM:SS); declared TEXT so TS dispatches String, not Time fuzzer.
climber.Country has 3 distinct over 10 rows (heavy duplication); mountain.Country 4 distinct incl. 'DR Congo Uganda' (space-joined multi-country).
mountain.Range only 3 distinct (Kilimanjaro/Mount Kenya/Rwenzori) over 7 rows; low-cardinality text.
mountain.Name contains parentheses, slashes, spaces ('Ngaliema / Mt Stanley (Margherita Pk)'); String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will not reproduce '/'.
Height/Prominence REAL with plausible 100-5900 range; Number fuzzer full range for REAL (scale from type args, none given) is far wider.
Points REAL small (6-15); Number fuzzer will draw from full [-10^scale,10^scale].
Mountain_ID/Climber_ID INT PKs, distinct==rows, no gaps in climber (1..10) but mountain has 7; TS fresh PKs are random ints, not sequential.
No composite keys, no self-FK, no dangling FK, no unique/check constraints, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
Mixed-case identifiers ('Mountain_ID','Name') require double-quoting; column lookup case-insensitive.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Mountain_ID/Climber_ID/Height/Prominence/Points: uniform over full type range then +-1/+-2 (int) or +-0.01/+-0.02 (float) perturbation; values implausible vs original (heights ~5000, points ~10).
String fuzzer on Name/Country/Range/Time: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings length 0-20 with 0.5 contaminate; will not match real names, 'DR Congo Uganda', or '1:13.05.6' format.
climber.Time declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, so no time-format preservation; queries filtering Time patterns will see garbage.
FK fill: climber.Mountain_ID drawn with replacement from mountain's FINAL Mountain_ID values; with small mountain size, ties/duplicates in child FK are likely (original has 5 distinct over 10).
PK dedup drops duplicate Mountain_ID/Climber_ID rows; with random ints over huge range collisions rare, so sizes stay near chosen n.
choose_table_sizes: 50% flat ~30-230 rows per table, else level-based (mountain level 0, climber level 1 x4); both far exceed 7/10 originals -> many more rows than original.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement: NULLs possible only if parent empty; otherwise all columns filled.
Likely FN driver: implausible numeric magnitudes (heights/points) make range predicates (Height>5000, Points>10) return wrong cardinality vs gold.
Likely FP driver: String fuzzer produces no ties/duplicates matching original low-cardinality Country/Range groupings, so GROUP BY / DISTINCT counts differ from gold.
FK ties: original climber.Mountain_ID has duplicates (5 distinct/10 rows); TS with replacement may or may not reproduce join multiplicities, affecting COUNT joins.
No Date/Time/Bool fuzzers exercised here (no such declared types); crash fallback not triggered (all types map to Number/String).
